shots.why: the account begins and fits the picture: gloves, hat, white dress, long boards. Every detail is read off this frame.
a different woman, no gloves, striped dress. The voice claims her without blinking. Same collection, not known to be the same people.
first contradiction, by picture: a man in a hat looks into the lens while she says her father isn't in any of them.
second: dark coat enters at the edge, in the first reel too. Nobody remarks on it.
return to a room. Slowed so the voice can have it. She lists what she can see, including the red chair at the bottom edge.
the camera turns and finds the icebox; still fits.
the exposure, no voice. It is a World's Fair exhibit, 1939: a brass rail, visitors in coats. The film does not repair this.
she keeps going, in a dirt yard with no house, another decade and another reel.
now the voice reads the contradiction aloud herself, and still doesn't stop.
a stranger's real smile under the line that least deserves it.
the child, who has no account of any of this, looks at whoever was really holding the camera.
